concept.overview: SonarQube is a platform for continuous inspection of code quality and security. A scanner analyzes your source code statically — without running it — and reports bugs, security vulnerabilities, and 'code smells' (maintainability issues), along with test coverage and duplication. Results are tracked over time on a dashboard, and a configurable Quality Gate turns those metrics into a pass/fail decision that CI/CD pipelines enforce, so quality problems are caught before they merge or ship.
concept.whyItMatters: Bugs and vulnerabilities are far cheaper to fix in review than in production. SonarQube shifts quality and security left, giving teams objective, trend-tracked metrics and an automated gate instead of relying on manual review alone. It is one of the most common code-quality tools in DevSecOps pipelines and a frequent interview topic.
useCases: Scanning every pull request for bugs, vulnerabilities, and code smells
Enforcing a Quality Gate that blocks merges/releases on failure
Tracking technical debt, coverage, and duplication over time
Standardizing rules across teams via shared Quality Profiles
Feeding security findings into a DevSecOps workflow
concept.architecture: SonarQube has three parts. A scanner runs in your build (SonarScanner CLI, or Maven/Gradle/CI plugins), analyzes the source using language-specific rules, and uploads results. The SonarQube server processes and stores those results in its database, computes metrics, and serves the web dashboard. A Quality Profile is the set of active rules applied to a language; a Quality Gate is a set of conditions on new code (e.g., no new bugs, coverage ≥ 80%, no new vulnerabilities) that yields a pass/fail status. The recommended 'Clean as You Code' model focuses the gate on new/changed code so quality improves incrementally. CI pipelines run the scanner and then check the gate via the API, failing the build if the gate is red.

bestPractices: Adopt 'Clean as You Code': gate on new code so quality improves without a huge backlog.
Run analysis on every PR and fail the build when the Quality Gate is red.
Import test coverage so the gate reflects real test quality, not just static rules.
Standardize Quality Profiles across teams for consistent rules.
Store the scanner token as a secret; never commit it.
pitfalls: Treating the dashboard as advisory and never failing the build on a red gate.
Gating on all legacy code at once, creating an unactionable mountain of debt.
Not importing coverage, so the gate misses untested code.
Committing the SonarQube token into the repository.
Chasing a green gate by disabling rules instead of fixing issues.
cheatSheet: Wait for gate in CI: sonar.qualitygate.wait=true
Focus on new code: Clean as You Code gate
Three issue types: bug, vulnerability, code smell

quiz.question: What does SonarQube primarily do?
options: Continuously inspect code quality and security via static analysis
quiz.explanation: SonarQube statically analyzes code for bugs, vulnerabilities, and code smells.

quiz.question: What is a Quality Gate?
options: Pass/fail conditions on metrics that CI enforces
quiz.explanation: A Quality Gate turns metrics into a pass/fail decision to block bad code.

quiz.question: Which are SonarQube's three main issue types?
quiz.explanation: SonarQube classifies issues as bugs, vulnerabilities, and code smells.

quiz.question: Static analysis inspects code without executing it.
quiz.explanation: SonarQube analyzes source statically, unlike running/dynamic tests.

quiz.question: What is the 'Clean as You Code' approach?
options: Gate on new/changed code so quality improves incrementally
quiz.explanation: Focusing the gate on new code avoids an unactionable backlog while steadily improving quality.

quiz.question: A PR introduces a new critical vulnerability. With a proper gate, what happens in CI?
options: The Quality Gate fails and the build is blocked
quiz.explanation: A red gate should fail the pipeline, preventing the merge until fixed.

quiz.question: Importing test coverage makes the Quality Gate reflect real test quality.
quiz.explanation: Without coverage data the gate can't judge how well new code is tested.

quiz.question: What is a Quality Profile?
options: The set of active analysis rules for a language
quiz.explanation: Quality Profiles define which rules are applied during analysis.

quiz.question: The team turns the gate green by disabling failing rules. Why is this bad?
options: It hides real issues instead of fixing them, defeating the purpose
quiz.explanation: Suppressing rules to pass the gate removes the signal the gate exists to provide.

quiz.question: Which setting makes the scanner wait for and honor the gate result in CI?
quiz.explanation: sonar.qualitygate.wait=true blocks until the gate result is known so CI can fail on red.

tasks.title: Run SonarQube and scan a project
tasks.goal: Get your first analysis on the dashboard.
steps: Start a SonarQube server (container) and log in
Create a project and generate a token
Run sonar-scanner against a small codebase
Explore the reported bugs, vulnerabilities, and smells
successCriteria: You can identify each issue type

tasks.title: Add coverage and a Quality Gate
steps: Generate test coverage and import it into the scan
Configure a Quality Gate on new code (e.g., coverage and no new bugs)
Introduce a deliberate issue and re-scan
successCriteria: The gate fails when the issue is present

tasks.title: Enforce the gate in CI
steps: Add a SonarQube analysis step to your pipeline
Set sonar.qualitygate.wait=true and store the token as a secret
Fail the build when the gate is red
successCriteria: A red gate fails the pipeline
The token is stored as a secret, not committed

tasks.title: Adopt Clean as You Code across a team
steps: Standardize a Quality Profile for the language
Configure gates focused on new code only
Wire PR analysis so results post back to the PR
Track debt and coverage trends over a few iterations
successCriteria: New code is gated without a legacy backlog blocking work
Quality trends are visible and improving
